question_text: Give any two microbes that are used in biotechnology.

insider_note: Two organisms, one mark each. Name both exactly — Escherichia coli and Agrobacterium tumefaciens — and add one line on what each is used for.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Escherichia coli
steps.margin_note: Name it, say it is the host, and name its plasmids as the vectors.
lines: ESCHERICHIA COLI is a bacterium used as the HOST
Its PLASMIDS — pBR322 and pUC19 — are used as
It multiplies quickly, so a cloned gene is copied
many times in a few hours.
steps.why: A host that divides every twenty minutes turns one recombinant cell into millions overnight, which is what makes gene cloning practical.
common_mistakes: Saying E. coli IS a plasmid. It is a BACTERIUM; its plasmids are the vectors. The guide's printed answer makes this mistake.
Saying the gene is put straight into the bacterium's own DNA. The gene is joined to a PLASMID first, and E. coli then takes that plasmid up.
steps.memory_tip: The bacterium is the host; its plasmid is the vector.

steps.label: Agrobacterium tumefaciens
steps.margin_note: Name it, name the Ti plasmid, and say it is the PLANT vector.

lines.text: E. coli hosts the gene; Agrobacterium carries

lines: Its TI PLASMID is used as a GENE TRANSFER
It has been disarmed, so it carries the gene in
steps.why: Agrobacterium already had a natural mechanism for pushing its own DNA into plant cells, so genetic engineers borrowed it rather than inventing one.
common_mistakes: Mixing up the two roles. The gene is first cloned in E. coli; then the disarmed Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium carries it into the plant cell.
Saying the Ti plasmid still causes tumours. It is DISARMED before use.
steps.memory_tip: Ti stands for tumour inducing, and it is disarmed before use.
